title: People illustration / Isometric character construction

location.series: IBM Design Language / alternate tab states
location.label: Isometric

slide_intent: Build a human figure from a stable structure before adding personality, because consistent proportions help viewers recognize a plausible person beneath stylization.
strategic_value: A repeatable progression from joints to clothing can keep IBM’s isometric people coherent without making every character identical.
demonstration: Four stages show one standing figure progressing from joint-and-line skeleton through volumetric construction and clothing outlines to a finished woman in a dark jacket and blue trousers.
practical_value: Use the construction stages to separate anatomy decisions from clothing, hair and color decisions.

ingredient.name: Isometric human construction
ingredient.role: Keep a stylized character proportionate while allowing individual identity.
ingredient.application: Start from the source’s eight-head-high skeleton and grid, then add organic curves, clothing and character details appropriate to the story.
ingredient.scope: People-illustration guidance. The shown figure is one example; the parent explicitly calls for diversity of bodies, ages, cultures and abilities.

reference_purposes.Intent: The accompanying People guidance says realistic proportions help audiences see themselves represented with respect.
reference_purposes.Application: The four stages demonstrate a reusable route from geometric skeleton to completed isometric character.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The parent anatomy guidance rejects caricature and unnecessary decoration while allowing slight grid deviations for organic features.
